messages:
maria: heads-up — we need a safe plan to migrate analytics.storage.table.event_meta.coercion from text -> jsonb (field name: event_metadata -> meta_v2). Console dashboards and quota queries hit this table a lot, so can't block reads. :eyes:

cella: is this the schema change where nested keys are being flattened out? any rough size delta expected?

maria: yes — meta_v2 will be a smaller, typed shape for the Console path (we drop a bunch of legacy keys). preliminary estimate: ~8% row size increase for jsonb storage, but we can remove some varchar columns later. main risk is index bloat and p99 query regressions on dashboard queries.

rick: short checklist idea: 1) add new column meta_v2 jsonb nullable + expression indexes for the two lookup paths 2) shadow-write from ingest (feature-flagged) 3) backfill in chunks 4) switch readers behind a flag 5) drop old column after monitoring. anyone worried about two writes?

andrew: auto-dualwrite = higher tail cost, but safer. for backfill we should use chunked updates with a throttled worker. avoid huge full-table transactions.

maria: agreed. proposal: add column, deploy ingest adapter to write meta_v2 when available (no failures if transform fails), start a continuous background backfill that updates 10k rows/hour per region, and route Console reads to meta_v2 behind a FF once 95% of active tenant rows have meta_v2 non-null.

cella: operational concerns: how do we measure "active tenant rows"? we should use last_30d event sampling and a light-weight audit table to track coverage. also need automated alert if Console p95 increases >10% during canary.

rick: SQL snippet for chunked backfill that I tested locally (use with care):

```sql
-- id is PK, batch_size param
WITH batch AS (
  SELECT id FROM analytics.storage.event_meta WHERE meta_v2 IS NULL LIMIT 500
)
UPDATE analytics.storage.event_meta e
SET meta_v2 = to_jsonb(transform_v1_to_v2(e.event_metadata::json))
FROM batch b
WHERE e.id = b.id
RETURNING e.id;
```

rick: run in a loop with an exponential backoff on errors and a rate limiter so we don't spike IO.

andrew: suggestion: create an expression index for queries that do jsonb_extract_path_text(meta_v2, 'user', 'id') — but only add indexes after a subset of rows are populated. otherwise index build cost is huge. consider CONCURRENTLY index creation.

maria: +1. plan: create column, deploy ingest-adapter, run shadow writes for two weeks in staging, start backfill in canary region, create indexes CONCURRENTLY once 50% coverage, flip Console readers via FF when 95% coverage + p95 stable, then schedule final cutover and drop old column after 30 days.

cella: do we need a compatibility proxy for any external consumers reading analytics.storage.event_meta? audit shows a few internal jobs directly query event_metadata. we should update them or keep a read adapter.

andrew: we can add a tiny read shim in db-adaptor: if meta_v2 present use it, else fallback to event_metadata. low-risk and transparent. add metrics for fallback rate.

infra-bot: migration-job queued: migration/1775518000-add-meta-v2 (scheduled window: 2026-04-04 02:00 UTC). See: https://ci.redwood/example/migrations/1775518000

maria: added owners: @cella for backfill orchestration, @rick for index strategy, @andrew for ingest/read adapter changes. I'll create the PR with the schema DDL and the canary runbook later today. :thumbsup:

cella: will add dashboard panels for coverage and fallback-rate, and an alert runbook.

andrew: will prototype ingest adapter in a feature branch and wire FF gating.

rick: will draft index timings and estimate IO cost for index builds — will prefer CONCURRENTLY.

maria: cool. small follow-up: if backfill pace is too slow we can increase batch size but cap IO to 200MB/s per region. keep the oncall notified before scale-ups.

cella: noted. tagging infra team for pre-approval: @infra-oncall please review the scheduled window.

infra-bot: infra-oncall notified (incident ref: MIG-1775518000).

maria: thanks — closing for now, will post progress updates in this thread. :boat:
